correctness.rationale: Exact one-vector sketched Galerkin formula is reduced to alpha+rho Z/chi_ell using Gaussian orthogonal invariance, with Z independent standard normal and chi_ell independent radius. The normalized ratio has the standard Student t law and an explicit positive density. Density integration gives the sharp log-tail constant for the approximation; fixed exact solution and reverse triangle give the same constant for actual error. Exponential integrability against polynomial density fails for every p>0. The eigendirection case is exactly solved. No finite enumeration is used to establish an infinite statement.

value.rationale: The source algorithm is used for expensive matrix-function actions and relies on high-probability embeddings. Exact sharp Student and logarithmic-error-tail laws reveal a real risk-management gap: even large finite oversampling gives no unconditional positive error moments when the initial vector is not an eigenvector, although typical sketched embeddings may succeed. This is a numerical structure/probabilistic reliability boundary, not a textbook-only restatement of the Student density.
